events.text: Peach Blossom Valley is in full bloom. Poets, painters and lovers fill the paths.

effects.log: Pink petals in your hair all day.
Your painting is mostly pink. It is accurate.

events.text: Legend says the valley's master lives on an island in the lake, guarded by a maze of peach trees.

ok.log: The master is an old man who laughs and teaches you a finger technique.

fail.log: You walk in circles until dusk. Beautiful circles.

effects.log: Blossoms drift on the water.

events.text: A wind shakes the trees and petals fall like rain.

choices.text: Practise sword forms in the petals

effects.log: Can you cut a falling petal? Almost.
Some moments are for standing in.

events.text: Lovers tie poems to a thousand-year-old peach tree.

effects.log: You write for someone. Maybe you will tell them.
A thousand kinds of love.

events.text: Bandits prey on the valley's rich visitors.

fail.log: A hard fight among the blossoms.

effects.log: Nobody is robbed on your paths.

events.text: Valley farmers make peach wine and sell it by the jar.

effects.log: Sweet and strong. (−3 taels)
Pink hands, free wine.

events.text: Under the blossoms you meet someone reading your favourite book.

effects.log: An afternoon becomes an evening.
Some things are best left perfect.

events.text: A famous painter asks you to pose for a painting of a wandering hero.

effects.log: The painting hangs in a lord's hall for a century.
The painting shows a tired traveller. It is his best work.

events.text: You climb a peach tree and eat the first peaches of the year. They are not ripe.

effects.log: A stomach ache to remember.
Patience. The sweetest peaches you ever tasted.

events.text: Behind a waterfall at the valley's end, a cave with a whole village inside, cut off from the world for centuries.

effects.log: They have never heard of any emperor. You leave the next morning unsure it was real.
You keep the promise all your life.

events.text: An old woman brews peach blossom tea for visitors.

effects.log: It tastes of spring.
She has lived here eighty springs and never left.

events.text: The petals fall. The valley turns green. The poets go home.

effects.log: Quieter, and just as beautiful.

choices.text: Go home with a pocket of petals

effects.log: They smell of spring for a month.
